easy.def: Silly in a fun way.
examples: A wacky hat.
The wacky clown made us laugh.
We had a wacky idea.

more.def: Funny, silly or very strange in a way that is fun.
examples: A wacky hat sat on the clown's head.
We had a wacky idea to wear our clothes backward.
The cartoon was full of wacky characters.

easy.def: A thick bunch of something pressed together.
examples: A wad of paper.
He had a wad of gum.
She held a wad of tissues.

more.def: A small, thick bunch of something soft or flat that is pressed or rolled together.
examples: He threw a wad of paper into the trash can.
She held a wad of tissues to her nose.
The baby had a wad of cotton in her hand.

easy.def: A flat breakfast cake with little square holes.
examples: I eat a waffle with syrup.
Dad made waffles.
The waffle has square holes.

more.def: A thin, crisp cake cooked in a special iron so that it has a pattern of little squares.
examples: We had waffles with strawberries and cream on Sunday morning.
He poured maple syrup into every square of his waffle.
The waffle iron clicked when the waffle was ready.

easy.def: Money you get for working.
examples: He earns a good wage.
The wage is small.
She got her wage.

more.def: The money that a worker is paid for each hour or each day of work.
examples: The store pays a fair wage to all its workers.
He saved his wage from the summer job to buy a bike.
The workers asked for a higher wage.

easy.def: Money that a person is paid for work.
examples: He earns good wages.
The wages are paid every week.
Her wages are low.

more.def: The money that a person is paid for work, usually counted by the hour or week.
examples: He earns good wages at the bakery.
The wages are paid every Friday.
The workers asked for higher wages.

easy.def: A cart with four wheels.
examples: I pulled a wagon.
The wagon is red.
We put the toys in the wagon.

more.def: A cart with four wheels that is pulled by hand or by an animal.
examples: The kids pulled the wagon to the park.
Settlers crossed the plains in covered wagons.
The farmer filled the wagon with hay.

easy.def: To cry out loudly in a long, sad sound.
examples: The baby began to wail.
The wind wailed at night.
The puppy wailed for its mom.

more.def: To make a long, high cry because you are sad or in pain, or to make a sound like that.
examples: The baby wailed until her mother picked her up.
The wind wailed through the cracks in the old barn.
A siren wailed in the distance as the fire truck sped by.

easy.def: A long, high, sad cry.
examples: I heard a wail.
The baby let out a wail.
The wail of the wind scared me.

more.def: A long, loud cry or sound that is sad or full of pain.
examples: A loud wail came from the toddler who dropped his ice cream.
The wail of the siren grew louder and louder.
We heard the wail of a wolf far away.

easy.def: The middle part of your body.
examples: The belt goes around my waist.
The water was up to my waist.
A band at the waist.

more.def: The part of the body between the ribs and the hips, where you wear a belt.
examples: The skirt was tight at the waist.
The water came up to her waist.
He tied a sash at his waist.

easy.def: To stay until something happens.
examples: Wait for me.
I waited at the door.
We wait for the bus.

more.def: To stay in a place or do nothing until something happens or someone comes.
examples: Please wait here until the teacher comes back.
We waited in line for an hour to ride the roller coaster.
I cannot wait for summer to come.

easy.def: A person who brings food to your table.
examples: The waiter brought the soup.
The waiter wrote down our order.
We thanked the waiter.

more.def: A person who takes orders and brings food to tables in a restaurant.
examples: The waiter brought us our soup.
The waiter carried five plates on one arm.
A waiter carried the plates on a tray.

easy.def: A woman who brings food to your table.
examples: The waitress brought our food.
The waitress was nice.
She is a waitress.

more.def: A woman who takes orders and serves food in a restaurant.
examples: The waitress brought our pancakes.
A waitress wrote down our order.
My aunt works as a waitress at a diner.

easy.def: To stop sleeping.
examples: I wake up at seven.
The baby woke early.
Dad wakes us with a song.

more.def: To stop sleeping, or to make someone stop sleeping.
examples: The sound of the rooster woke us at dawn.
I set an alarm to wake me up before school.
Please do not wake the baby.

easy.def: To move on your legs, one step after another.
examples: I walk to school.
The baby walked.
We walk the dog.

more.def: To move along on foot at a normal speed, putting one foot in front of the other.
examples: We walk to the library every Saturday.
The baby walked across the room for the first time.
He walked the dog around the block.

easy.def: A trip on foot.
examples: We took a walk.
It is a short walk.
I love a walk in the park.

more.def: A trip made on foot, for fun or exercise.
examples: After dinner, we went for a walk along the river.
It is a short walk from our house to the school.
The nature walk was full of bird songs.

easy.def: When people leave work or a meeting together as a protest.
examples: The workers had a walkout.
A walkout began.
The walkout ended.

more.def: When a group of people leave their work, a meeting or a school together to protest something.
examples: The workers staged a walkout to ask for fair pay.
Students held a walkout to ask for a safer crosswalk.
The walkout ended when the leaders met.

easy.def: A side of a room or building.
examples: The picture is on the wall.
Paint the wall.
She leaned against the wall.

more.def: One of the sides of a room or building.
examples: We hung a map on the wall.
The wall of the classroom is covered with drawings.
Ivy climbed up the garden wall.

easy.def: A tall side of stone or brick around a place.
examples: A wall goes around the castle.
The garden has a stone wall.
We walked along the old town wall.

more.def: A solid barrier of stone or brick that goes around or divides a place.
examples: A tall stone wall surrounds the old castle.
The garden wall keeps the rabbits out.
A wall once protected the old city.

easy.def: A small, flat case for money and cards.
examples: Dad put money in his wallet.
My wallet is in my pocket.
She lost her wallet.

more.def: A small, flat case for carrying paper money and cards in your pocket or bag.
examples: He pulled a dollar out of his wallet.
The wallet had a picture of her family inside.
I found a wallet on the sidewalk and gave it to the teacher.

easy.def: To roll around in mud or water.
examples: The pig wallowed in the mud.
Hippos wallow in water.
The buffalo wallowed.

more.def: To roll around in mud or water for pleasure, as large animals do to keep cool.
examples: The pigs wallowed in the cool mud on the hot afternoon.
Hippos wallow in the river to stay cool.
The buffalo wallowed in the dust and rolled over.

easy.def: Paper with a pattern that is put on walls.
examples: The wallpaper has flowers.
We put up new wallpaper.
The wallpaper is blue.

more.def: Paper with a pattern or picture that is stuck to the walls of a room.
examples: The wallpaper in my room has stars on it.
Mom put up new wallpaper with stripes.
The old wallpaper was peeling from the wall.

easy.def: A nut with a hard, wrinkled shell.
examples: I cracked a walnut.
Squirrels eat walnuts.
Mom put walnuts in the cake.

more.def: A nut with a hard, wrinkled shell that grows on a tall tree and is often eaten in baking or on its own.
examples: The squirrel carried a walnut up the tree to eat it.
Grandma baked banana bread with chopped walnuts on top.
A walnut tree grew beside the old farmhouse.

easy.def: A graceful dance in three beats.
examples: They danced a waltz.
The waltz is slow.
The waltz is pretty.

more.def: A smooth, gliding dance with a beat of three counts.
examples: They danced a waltz at the party.
The orchestra played a slow waltz.
The waltz has a rhythm of one, two, three.

easy.def: A thin stick used by a magician.
examples: The magician waved the wand.
A wand is magic.
I have a wand.

more.def: A thin stick that a magician or fairy waves to do magic.
examples: The magician waved his wand and a rabbit appeared.
The fairy's wand sparkled with glitter.
I made a wand from a stick for the play.

easy.def: To walk around with no place to go.
examples: We wander in the park.
The cows wander in the field.
Do not wander away from me.

more.def: To move around slowly without a clear direction or purpose.
examples: The lost puppy wandered through the streets.
We wandered around the market looking at the stalls.
His mind wandered during the long speech.

easy.def: To wish to have or do something.
examples: I want a drink.
She wants to play.
We wanted to see the show.

more.def: To feel that you would like to have, do, or be something.
examples: I want to be a vet when I grow up.
My little brother wants a story before bed.
They wanted a bigger garden, so they dug up the lawn.

easy.def: A big fight between countries.
examples: Soldiers came home when the war was over.
We read a book about a war long ago.
My great-grandfather talked about the war.

more.def: A long period of fighting between countries or groups of people.
examples: The war lasted for four years before peace was made.
Museums in my city tell about a war that happened long ago.
After the war, many families began to rebuild their towns.

easy.def: A part of a hospital.
examples: The children's ward is bright.
The nurse works in the ward.
My brother was in the ward.

more.def: A large room or part of a hospital with beds for patients.
examples: The children's ward has toys and books.
The nurse walked through the ward.
He stayed in the ward for two days.

easy.def: A person in charge of a place or area.
examples: The park warden helped.
The game warden watched the lake.
A warden guarded the woods.

more.def: A person who takes care of a park, wild area or building.
examples: The warden looked after the nature reserve.
A game warden checked fishing permits.
The warden counted the birds.

easy.def: A tall cupboard for clothes.
examples: My clothes are in the wardrobe.
The wardrobe is big.
The wardrobe door creaks.

more.def: A tall cupboard in which you hang your clothes, or all the clothes you own.
examples: My coats hang in the wardrobe.
The wardrobe door creaked open.
She has a large wardrobe of winter clothes.

easy.def: A big building for storing things.
examples: The boxes are in the warehouse.
The warehouse is huge.
The truck went to the warehouse.

more.def: A large building where goods are stored before they are sold.
examples: The boxes were stored in a warehouse.
Trucks lined up at the warehouse.
The warehouse was full of toys.

easy.def: Fighting between countries.
examples: We read about warfare long ago.
Warfare is sad.
The soldiers learned about warfare.

more.def: The fighting between countries or armies during a war, and the ways that they fight.
examples: In history class we learned about how warfare changed from swords to tanks.
Castles were built to protect people during warfare long ago.
Many people work for peace so that there is no more warfare.

easy.def: A man in stories who does magic.
examples: The warlock cast a spell.
A warlock lives in the woods.
The warlock had a staff.

more.def: A male magic user in stories, often a wicked one.
examples: The warlock cast a spell on the village.
In the tale, a warlock lived in a tower.
The warlock stirred a bubbling pot.

easy.def: A little hot.
examples: The soup is warm.
She has a warm blanket.
It is warm in the sun.

more.def: Pleasantly hot, not cold and not too hot.
examples: We sat on the warm sand.
She wrapped herself in a warm blanket.
The warm bread came out of the oven.

easy.def: To make less cold.
examples: Warm your hands by the fire.
Soup warms me up.
She warmed the milk.

more.def: To make something less cold, or to become less cold.
examples: He warmed his hands by the campfire.
The sun warmed the sand.
Soup warms you up on a cold day.

easy.def: In a friendly way.
examples: She greeted us warmly.
He smiled warmly.
They welcomed us warmly.

more.def: In a kind and friendly way, or in a way that keeps you warm.
examples: She greeted us warmly at the door.
He thanked the helpers warmly.
She dressed warmly for the snow.

easy.def: The feeling of being nice and warm.
examples: I felt the warmth of the sun.
The fire gave warmth.
She felt the warmth of the blanket.

more.def: The quality or feeling of being warm, or of being kind and friendly.
examples: We sat close to the fire to feel its warmth.
The warmth of the sun made the cat fall asleep.
Her warmth made the new students feel welcome.

easy.def: To tell someone about danger.
examples: The sign warns us that the floor is wet.
Mom warned me the pan was hot.
The bell warns us of a fire.

more.def: To tell someone about a possible danger or problem before it happens.
examples: The lifeguard warned the swimmers about the strong waves.
Dark clouds warned us that a storm was coming.
The sign warns drivers of a sharp turn ahead.

easy.def: A sign that danger is near.
examples: The sign is a warning.
He gave me a warning.
The storm warning.

more.def: A sign or message that tells you of a danger.
examples: The sign gave a warning about thin ice.
The storm warning came on the radio.
The coach gave us a warning to stop talking.

easy.def: To bend out of shape.
examples: The wood will warp.
The board warped in the rain.
The record warped.

more.def: To bend or twist out of its usual shape, as wood does when it gets wet.
examples: The wooden door warped in the damp.
Rain can warp wooden floors.
The old record warped in the heat.

easy.def: Bent or twisted out of shape.
examples: The board is warped.
A warped record.
The door is warped.

more.def: Bent or twisted out of its natural shape, often because of heat or damp.
examples: The wooden board was warped after it got wet.
The door was warped and would not close.
A warped record plays with a wobbling sound.

easy.def: A brave fighter in old times.
examples: The warrior was brave.
The warrior carried a shield.
The warrior fought for his tribe.

more.def: A person who fights bravely in battle, especially in the past.
examples: The warrior carried a shield and a spear.
In the story, the brave warrior protected the village.
The warriors wore armor.

easy.def: A small, hard bump on the skin.
examples: I have a wart on my finger.
A wart is small.
The wart went away.

more.def: A small, hard bump on the skin that is caused by a virus and usually goes away by itself.
examples: I had a wart on my finger, but it went away after a few months.
A wart is a small, rough bump on the skin.
Toads do not cause warts, even though they have bumpy skin.

easy.def: To clean with water.
examples: Wash your hands.
We wash the dishes.
Dad washed the car.

more.def: To clean something using water and often soap.
examples: Wash your hands before dinner.
We washed the dog in the tub.
Mom washes clothes on Mondays.

easy.def: A machine that washes clothes.
examples: Put it in the washer.
The washer is running.
Our washer is new.

more.def: A machine that washes clothes or dishes, or a small flat ring of metal or rubber that fits under a screw or a bolt.
examples: Mom put the dirty clothes into the washer.
The dishwasher cleaned all the plates after dinner.
Dad put a small metal washer under the nut.

easy.def: A room with a toilet and a sink.
examples: Where is the washroom?
The washroom is clean.
I need the washroom.

more.def: A room with a sink and a toilet, also called a bathroom or restroom.
examples: Excuse me, where is the washroom?
The washroom is down the hall on the left.
Wash your hands in the washroom before lunch.

easy.def: A flying insect with a thin waist that can sting.
examples: A wasp stung me.
The wasp has stripes.
A wasp built a nest.

more.def: A flying insect with a narrow waist and yellow and black stripes that can sting, and often builds a paper nest.
examples: A wasp built a paper nest under the roof of our porch.
The wasp buzzed around the picnic table.
Wasps look like bees, but they have thinner bodies.

easy.def: To use too much of something.
examples: Do not waste water.
I wasted my time.
She wastes paper.

more.def: To use something carelessly or for no good reason.
examples: Turn off the tap so you do not waste water.
He wasted the whole morning playing games.
We waste less food when we plan our meals.

easy.def: Things you throw away.
examples: Put waste in the bin.
Waste goes to the dump.
Food waste goes in the compost.

more.def: Things that are thrown away because they are no longer wanted.
examples: The truck takes our waste to the dump.
Plastic waste can hurt sea animals.
We sort our waste into recycling and trash.

easy.def: To look at something for a while.
examples: I watch the birds.
We watched a movie.
Watch me jump.

more.def: To look carefully at something for a while.
examples: We sat on the dock and watched the boats go by.
She watched the chef roll out the dough.
Watch the clock so we do not miss the bus.

easy.def: A small clock you wear on your wrist.
examples: I got a new watch.
His watch says noon.
She looks at her watch.

more.def: A small clock that you wear on your wrist.
examples: He checked his watch to see if it was time for lunch.
My grandfather gave me his old watch.
The watch ticked quietly on her wrist.

easy.def: A person who guards a building at night.
examples: The watchman walked around.
A watchman guards the store.
The watchman checked the doors.

more.def: A person whose job is to guard a building or a place, especially at night.
examples: The watchman walked around the warehouse with a flashlight each night.
In the old town, the watchman called out the hours from the tower.
The watchman locked the gates when everyone had gone home.

easy.def: What falls as rain and fills rivers and oceans.
examples: I drink water.
The water is cold.
Fish live in water.

more.def: The clear liquid that falls as rain, fills rivers and oceans, and is needed by all living things.
examples: Plants and animals need water to live.
The water in the lake was cold and clear.
We filled our bottles with water before the hike.

easy.def: To give plants a drink.
examples: I water the plants.
She watered the garden.
Dad waters the lawn.

more.def: To give plants or soil a drink so they can grow.
examples: We water the tomato plants every morning.
He watered the flowers with a green can.
The farmer waters the crops during the dry summer.

easy.def: Water that falls over a high place.
examples: We saw a waterfall.
The waterfall is tall.
We swam by the waterfall.

more.def: A place where a river or stream drops from a high place, such as a cliff, to a lower one.
examples: We hiked to a tall waterfall deep in the forest.
The waterfall roared as it crashed onto the rocks below.
A rainbow shimmered in the mist of the waterfall.

easy.def: A big, juicy fruit that is green outside and red inside.
examples: I ate watermelon.
The watermelon is sweet.
We cut the watermelon.

more.def: A large, round, juicy fruit with a hard green skin, sweet red flesh and many black seeds.
examples: We ate cold watermelon at the picnic on the hot summer day.
The watermelon was so big that I could not lift it.
He had a contest to see who could spit a watermelon seed the farthest.

easy.def: A moving hill of water.
examples: The wave hit the shore.
Big waves splash.
We jumped over the waves.

more.def: A moving ridge of water on the sea or a lake.
examples: The wave crashed against the rocks.
We jumped over the small waves.
Big waves pull the surfers out to sea.

easy.def: To move your hand to say hello or goodbye.
examples: I wave to my friend.
She waved goodbye.
He waves at the bus.

more.def: To move your hand back and forth to greet someone or say goodbye.
examples: The children waved to the bus driver.
She waved goodbye from the window.
He waved a flag at the parade.

easy.def: To shake or move back and forth.
examples: The candle wavered.
His voice wavered.
I did not waver.

more.def: To shake or move back and forth, or to be unsure.
examples: The candle flame wavered in the wind.
His voice wavered as he spoke.
She did not waver in her choice.

easy.def: A soft stuff that candles are made of.
examples: The candle is made of wax.
The wax melted.
I polished the floor with wax.

more.def: A soft, oily substance that melts easily and is used for candles and polish.
examples: The candle was made of wax.
The hot wax dripped onto the plate.
Dad rubbed wax on the car.

easy.def: A path or road to get somewhere.
examples: This is the way to school.
Which way did the cat go?
The way home is short.

more.def: A road or path that leads somewhere, or the direction you go to get there.
examples: Can you tell me the way to the library?
The sign pointed the other way, so we turned around.
It is a long way to the top of the mountain.

easy.def: How you do something.
examples: I like your way of drawing.
Mom showed me a new way to tie shoes.
There is a way to fix it.

more.def: The method or manner in which something is done.
examples: There is more than one way to solve this math problem.
My grandfather has a funny way of laughing.
Birds find their way home by using the sun and the stars.
